transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been struggling because I’ve lost all interest in the hobbies I used to enjoy. I also find it incredibly difficult to get any motivation to finish my daily tasks, and this has been going on for about a year and a half now.
Have you felt this way nearly every day for the past year and a half, or have there been periods of a few months or longer where you felt completely like your normal self?
It’s been this way consistently for a year and 7 months. I haven't had any periods where I felt like my normal self during that time.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder]. Given the patient reports a consistent duration of symptoms for 19 months without any period of feeling like their normal self, Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) becomes the primary consideration as it specifically requires a duration of at least two years in adults (or one year in children/adolescents), and the patient's presentation aligns with this chronic, unremitting course.
